blindSummary: For trans visitors the picture here is a wide gap between statute and practice. A 2020 penal code decriminalised same-sex conduct AND prohibited discrimination based on sexual orientation — one of the stronger such statutory packages on paper in the region. A 2024 shadow report by domestic LGBT organisations documents the gap: discrimination persists across health, education and employment; trans people have no legal gender recognition; and violence goes under-investigated. The capital has a visible, organised community.
blindOutOfScope: Statutory protections vs implementation gap documented by domestic civil-society organisations.
blindSourceSummaries: Shadow report to a regional human-rights commission (81st session, Oct-Nov 2024) by domestic LGBTIQ organisations (five named groups plus others), produced with a national NGO and a regional LGBTI federation. Documents discrimination and stigma, violence, barriers to healthcare including gender-affirming care, and obstacles to access to justice for LGBTQI+ people in this country, with recommendations to the government.

Submission by domestic organisations to the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (74th pre-session). Addresses discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, barriers LGBT people face in accessing sexual and reproductive health, comprehensive sexuality education, gender-affirming care and education, and the lack of government-generated data on LGBT people in this country.

Strategic-litigation-centre chapter on transgender rights in this country (from a regional legal-review volume on laws and policies affecting transgender persons): constitutional rights mapping (the equality article does not list gender or sexual orientation among prohibited discrimination grounds, but 'other status' should be read to include them per the UN Human Rights Committee); no specific law for gender-marker change, though a provision of the 2015 civil-registration code gives the registrar general authority to alter records; employment discrimination prohibited under the 2015 labour law.

Online magazine (Oct 2019): overview of changing LGBTQ+ rights across the continent - 34 of 54 countries criminalise homosexuality; discusses the 'white person's problem' framing used to dismiss queer rights in one large regional country and the thorny, contested nature of legal change (context including this country and one regional peer).

Foreign broadcaster (April 2012): the rise of a trans star - a trans woman singer/dancer who is the face of the country's popular indigenous rap-techno dance-music genre, named best artist in that genre for 2011 and booked to perform at a high-profile presidential concert series - notable visibility for a trans person in a country where homosexuality was then illegal.

An LGBTQ+ news outlet (Feb 2021): this country decriminalised homosexuality - the new penal code (adopted January 2019, effective February 2021) removed the historic 'vice against nature' ban and introduced anti-discrimination protection, with discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation punishable by prison.
blindLocalsOnly: Trans people have no legal gender recognition; the implementation gap (health, education, employment discrimination, under-investigated violence) falls on residents.
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct is decriminalised and sexual-orientation discrimination prohibited — of direct concern mainly to trans visitors who have relationships or are perceived as same-sex-active while travelling.
